title: Sustainable Cities: Transport Maths
welcome_lead: Compare modal carbon, calculate transport emissions and plan greener commutes.
meta_desc: GCSE Environmental Science adventure on city transport calculations: modal emissions and modal shift.
final_note: You can now redesign a commute and slash its footprint.

concepts.def: Proportion of trips using each transport mode.
Grams of CO2 emitted per kilometre travelled.
Walking and cycling; zero direct emissions.
Driving to a hub then taking public transport.
Moving trips from one mode to a greener mode.
Fee for driving in busy zones to cut traffic.

walkthroughs.body_html: Typical UK gCO2 per passenger-km: car about 170, bus 100, train 35, cycling and walking zero direct. Cars dominate short trips that could shift to active travel. Filling buses and trains lowers per-passenger emissions further. Choosing mode by trip purpose, distance and load gives biggest cuts.

Daily emissions = distance x emission factor. A 20 km car commute at 170 gCO2/km gives 3400 g or 3.4 kg per single journey, so 6.8 kg per round trip. Over 220 working days that is around 1500 kg CO2 per year. Switching to bus at 100 gCO2/km cuts the yearly figure to about 880 kg.

Cities use congestion charges (London), low emission zones, cycle lanes, free bus passes, mobility-as-a-service apps and dense mixed-use planning. London's congestion charge cut central traffic by around 30 percent. Paris '15-minute city' planning aims for all essentials within a short walk or cycle.
